assurance

uh-SHOOR-uhns · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Assurance is a confident guarantee; certainty that something will happen.

The mechanic gave us her assurance that the car would be ready by Friday.

Worked Example

Even after the landlord's written assurance that the heat would be fixed, the tenants kept their space heaters plugged in.

The landlord offered a confident promise -- a guarantee -- that the repair would happen. That promise is an assurance, whether or not the tenants chose to trust it.

Antonyms

doubt

How Strong Is It? — promise → assurance → guarantee

promise vs. assurance

promise vs. assurance: A promise says you intend to do something -- an assurance goes further, expressing confident certainty that it will happen.

guarantee vs. assurance

guarantee vs. assurance: A guarantee is the strongest form -- a formal commitment, often backed by consequences if it's broken, while an assurance may rest only on someone's word.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — as-

prefix — as-: to, toward (a form of ad-) (Latin)

root — sur-

root — sur-: safe, certain (Latin (securus))

suffix — -ance

suffix — -ance: noun-forming: the state or act of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: As- ('to') + sur- ('safe, certain') + -ance: an assurance is the act of making someone certain -- handing them a safe, confident guarantee.

Root Check

Word Choice

Assurance is about confidence and certainty: you speak with assurance, or give someone your assurance. Don't confuse it with insurance, the paid financial product -- insurance is a contract; an assurance is a confident promise.
